A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of constrained regularization analysis in low-angle quasi- elastic light scattering is feasible, but the procedure is not yet fully developed.

the constrained regularization analysis of low-angle quasi- elastic light scattering data can be a valuable tool in the study of colloidal systems, provided that the data are properly collected and that a suitable regularization constraint is applied.

the constrained regularization procedure is an efficient means of determining particle size distributions from low-angle quasi- elastic light scattering data when the following precautions are observed: (1) the correlation function is obtained from a short time period of data acquisition; (2) the mean photon counting rates are stable during the period of photon count accumulation; (3) the photon count data are not autocorrelated until the transient effects of the mean photon counting have been removed from the raw photon count data.
